target_customer: Engineering and manufacturing teams in construction, automotive, aerospace and fabrication that produce 2D drawings from 3D CAD models
problem: Engineers manually create manufacturing drawings for each part, which is slow and error prone.
business_model: B2B software subscription and pilots, integrating with Inventor and SolidWorks

founders.name: Mohammed Al-arnawoot
founders.background_notes: YC page: director of engineering at Dozr and VP of engineering at Emagin, which was acquired by Innovyze.

founders.name: Abdullah Elqabbany
founders.background_notes: YC page: electromechanical engineer who worked as a drafter and led manufacturing process automation.

founders.name: Tahsin Rahman
education: University of Toronto, PhD in electrical and computer engineering
founders.background_notes: YC page: led a cybersecurity AI team for the department and earlier worked on oil and gas instrumentation.

technical_complexity.rationale: Learning layout, dimensioning and annotation conventions across CAD platforms and matching company templates is hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Learned customer templates and CAD plugin integration create stickiness, but CAD vendors can build the same feature.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Autodesk added AI automated drawings to Fusion in October 2024, about nine months after the batch. No acquisition of Draftaid was found.

market_need_then: Engineers described drawing creation as repetitive work, and the founders reported paid pilots with contracts valued at $150,000 by early 2024.

branding.domain_note: Uses draftaid.io, not draftaid.com. History not found.

identity.logo: Black logo with blue accent graphics
identity.visual_style: Clean minimal layout with emoji style industry icons
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct productivity claims about consistent 2D drawings from 3D models

brand_strength.rationale: Name states the function clearly, but no press about the brand was found, and capitalization is inconsistent (DraftAid, Draftaid, DraftAId).

outcome_analysis: Draftaid is a Toronto YC W24 company whose founders combine drafting, engineering management and a PhD in AI. It reported paid pilots worth $150,000 and later claimed about 180,000 drawings generated in 2025, a company figure. Autodesk's own AI drawings feature in October 2024 is the clearest incumbent threat, and no verified funding beyond YC was found.
notes: Aggregators list a $500K round from Y Combinator in January or February 2024 (a convertible note per CB Insights, pre-seed per VCBacked); this is the YC deal and is not recorded as a round. A Canadian AI Compute Access Fund grant record exists but the amount was not seen. No dated competitor sources near January 2024 were found, so the list is empty. Drawing volume claims come from a Xometry interview summarized by search and are company claims. Founding year is 2023 per LinkedIn and CB Insights while one source says 2022. Completeness pass: the YC deal of US$500K per company is recorded as an other round, dated 2024-02 per Seedtable and VCBacked (CB Insights says a convertible note on 2024-01-01); the University of Waterloo news item reports the amount for DraftAid and its Winter 2024 peers.
